zones.name: ExtractionState route/ok multi-writer cascade
zones.description: The ingestion pipeline threads a single mutable ExtractionState through a 10-gate evaluation, a GateSpec-driven recovery loop, two post-loop 'quality check' rerouters, and a match-based persistence dispatcher. finalize_gate_and_route() is documented as the 'single writer' of gate_result/ok/reason/first_defect/route, but six other call sites write state.route and/or state.ok directly, leaving the five fields mutually inconsistent. Every downstream consumer (reject reason, all_defects sidecar field, flat-vs-tree persistence, LOW_QUALITY_TREES metric label) reads a different subset of those fields, so any change to one stage silently reinterprets the others.
zones.mechanism: There is no invariant tying state.ok to state.gate_result. finalize_gate_and_route derives route from first_defect via decide_route, but _recover_rtl_flat_compare (recovery.py:593), _recover_vlm_fallback (recovery.py:649/667/685), _recover_flat_prefer (recovery.py:728-729) and _recover_landscape_reroute (recovery.py:758-759) assign state.route = Route.FLAT (the last two also assign state.ok = False) with an explicit comment in index() that there is 'no re-derivation afterwards'. A tree that passed every gate therefore reaches the dispatcher with ok=False, route=FLAT, first_defect=TreeDefect.OK (value ''), and gate_result.ok=True. If _persist_flat_result then returns None, index() computes _reject_reason = state.first_defect.value == '' and raises LowQualityTreeError('') / increments LOW_QUALITY_TREES.labels(reason=''). Meanwhile _persist_tree_result writes meta['all_defects'] from the stale gate_result, so the sidecar records a clean tree for a rejected document. Because the recovery loop also re-enters finalize_gate_and_route from inside recovery methods, later loop iterations evaluate eligibility against post-recovery state rather than the original gate result, so gate ordering and recovery ordering are coupled: any reorder of GATES changes which recovery sees which tree. Fixing one writer (the classic 'make finalize_gate_and_route authoritative' patch) reverts whatever behaviour the other five were compensating for, which is why RFC-036 D3, RFC-029 D1, RFC-033 D8 and RFC-035 D2 each added a new override instead of removing one.
zones.evidence_history: Chain 'RFC-040 D2 reordered the verdict promotion pipeline from six independent _try_* guards into a precedence-locked cascade' (~8 documents shifted MARGINAL/PASS -> FAIL); chain 'GATE_TABLE in validate_tree evaluates garbling (severity=0) before node_count_lower_bound' (RFC-040 D4, open since OCR_IMAGE_BLOCK_CONFLATION_INVESTIGATION 2026-07-27); chain 'verdict.py fix #3 (cf904ff): _try_image_enrichment returns None instead of MARGINAL'; chain 'Verdict gate promotion cascade: _try_cat_a path lacked effectively_garbled guard'; chain 'OCR recovery eligibility check only inspected first_defect'; chain 'Four independent regression fixes ... combined effect ~40 documents re-evaluated'. Theme: 'Verdict/garble/OCR-recovery form a tightly coupled triad where a fix to one leg reliably flips outcomes in the others ... discovered only via corpus re-ingestion audits, not pre-merge tests.' Zone-1/2/3/6/8 fix labels appear 15 times across gates.py and verdict.py docstrings.
zones.evidence_code: helpers/types.py:355-388 finalize_gate_and_route docstring: 'Single writer of gate_result/ok/reason/first_defect/route on *state*. ... Every call site that previously set a subset of these fields ... must call this instead.' Contradicted by client/recovery.py:593, 649, 667, 685, 728-729, 758-759 which assign state.route/state.ok directly. client/indexer.py:1473-1475 comment: 'Quality checks (may override route intentionally - no re-derivation afterwards).' client/indexer.py:1521 computes _reject_reason = state.first_defect.value, and helpers/types.py TreeDefect.OK = '' so the reject reason and Prometheus label are the empty string on the flat-prefer/landscape-reroute path. client/indexer.py:1279 writes meta['all_defects'] from the un-refreshed state.gate_result. client/indexer.py:1454-1470 recovery loop mutates state in place and relies on recovery methods calling finalize_gate_and_route internally.

zones.name: Normalize-before-detect null-detector lattice (presentation forms / NFKC)
zones.description: The Arabic presentation-forms signal (U+FB50-FDFF, U+FE70-FEFF) is destroyed by NFKC normalization early in the pipeline, but four independent detectors are wired to consume it downstream: Gate 7 (_gate_bidi_degraded), detect_garble's PF recovery branch, _garble_check_nodes' per-node contexts, and _try_image_enrichment's garble re-check. Every fallback path that supplies the flag operates on post-NFKC text and therefore returns False structurally, not empirically. The detectors report zero violations, and that zero has repeatedly been read as evidence of safety.
zones.mechanism: had_presentation_forms has exactly one true producer: _renormalize_bidi_guarded (indexer.py:180-183), which captures the flag pre-NFKC on the remote Docling path only, and which returns an explicit had_presentation_forms=False sentinel when the bilingual Latin guard trips (indexer.py:155-161) - i.e. exactly on the mixed Arabic/English documents that the Run-20 regressions were about. Every other producer is a fallback that cannot see the signal: _infer_presentation_forms' own docstring states 'Post-NFKC this ratio is always 0', yet it is the flag source at 8 call sites including tree_validation.py:392 (which feeds Gate 7 and Gate 4) and verdict.py:257. decide_rtl never assigns had_presentation_forms at all, so its RtlDecision always carries the dataclass default False - and validate_tree falls back to decide_rtl(sig.flat_text) whenever rtl_decision is not threaded in. Recovery then actively destroys the one live carrier: _execute_ocr_retry sets state.rtl_decision = None on the non-remote branch (recovery.py:332) and _recover_vlm_fallback clears it 'so validate_tree recomputes' - after which the recompute is structurally blind. Finally the NFKC-recovery heuristic inside detect_garble compares _effective_script == 'Arabic' (garble.py:583), a string this codebase never produces: _infer_script returns only 'Arab', 'Latn' or None, and 'Arabic' occurs exactly once in the whole source tree, at that comparison. So the fallback intended to recover the destroyed signal is dead code. Any fix that makes one detector actually fire (RFC-040 D5 did this for the garble gate) immediately hard-fails a class of documents the other, still-blind detectors had been passing - which is precisely the PASS->ERROR / MARGINAL->ERROR regression pattern.
zones.evidence_history: Chain 'ocr_langs.py fix #2 (cf904ff / RFC-040 D5) ... MOU MOHRE went PASS(Run19)->ERROR(Run20)'; chain 'garble.py fix #1 (cf904ff): improved Arabic presentation-forms/NFKC detection ... check presentation-forms *before* decomposition destroys the signal'; chain '_check_bidi_coherence gate ... RFC-033 F2 still open at POST-FIX-WAVE3'; chain 'D2 Part A guard (_heading_is_logical_order)'; chain 'Garble detection kernel: presentation-forms fallback with NFKC blind spot in verdict.py removed'; chain 'Wave 2 triage spec for garble-detection kernel marked as redundant'. Themes: 'Null-detector pattern: multiple quality gates ... structurally cannot fire on their real failure mode ... yet their zero violations measurement was historically read as evidence of safety and used to justify enabling stricter enforcement defaults (e.g. BIDI_COHERENCE_ENFORCE=true)' and 'NFKC normalisation blind spot in garble detection'.
zones.evidence_code: helpers/garble.py:30-45 _infer_presentation_forms docstring: 'Post-NFKC this ratio is always 0 (the codepoints decompose into logical Arabic), so callers on post-normalization text correctly get False'; it is nevertheless the flag source at helpers/tree_validation.py:392, helpers/verdict.py:257, helpers/garble.py:855, client/indexer.py:513, client/indexer.py:998, client/indexer.py:1024, client/images.py:135, converters/pictures.py:21. script.py:694-708 RtlDecision.had_presentation_forms defaults to False and decide_rtl (script.py) never sets it; helpers/tree_validation.py:396-398 falls back to decide_rtl(sig.flat_text). client/recovery.py:332 'state.rtl_decision = None' and recovery.py:634-636 clear the only live carrier. helpers/garble.py:583 'elif _arc > 0 and _pf == 0 and _effective_script == "Arabic"' - verified by grep that the literal "Arabic" appears exactly once in src/pageindex_mcp/, while script.py:174 shows _infer_script returns only 'Arab'/'Latn'/None. client/indexer.py:155-161 bilingual guard returns RtlDecision(method='bilingual_guard_skip') with the flag left False.

zones.name: Split verdict authority: five writers over two stores
zones.description: The authoritative verdict for a document is written by five independent code paths across two stores (MinIO sidecar processed/<id>.meta.json and the Postgres doc_registry row), with only one of them enforcing the max-priority-wins CAS. The others are unconditional read-merge-writes. Which value survives depends on process boundaries and timing, not on any single arbiter.
zones.mechanism: The verdict is computed inside the isolated converters_cli child, which by design has no Postgres pool, so _persist_tree_result / _persist_flat_result write it optimistically and unconditionally to the sidecar via save_doc_meta. The worker parent then runs _upsert_registry_row, which performs the real CAS (_UPSERT_SQL VERDICT_PRIORITY guard) and best-effort backfills the sidecar with the winning row - so the same key is written twice per ingest, the second write authoritative and capable of silently reverting the first. Three further writers exist: registry_backfill/reconcile.py, registry_backfill/backfill.py (sidecar-only self-heal, no CAS), and promotion_sweep.py (save_doc_meta + upsert_doc). The load-bearing false belief is that save_doc_meta itself arbitrates: registry_backfill/backfill.py:145 states 'The CAS guard in save_doc_meta protects against clobbering a newer verdict', but save_doc_meta contains no priority comparison at all - it merges 'verdict' from meta over existing in a plain _MERGE_FIELDS loop, and its own docstring removed the write-visibility barrier ('Consistency: eventual - no _confirm_write_visible call'). Layered on top, force_verdict_override selects a second SQL statement (_UPSERT_OVERRIDE_SQL) that bypasses the priority CAS while keeping the processed_at CAS, so there are two arbitration semantics per table. Consequence: a re-ingestion producing a lower-priority verdict is discarded by Postgres but may still land in the sidecar (if the parent backfill fails or the doc is touched by backfill/promotion_sweep), and corpus audits that read sidecars see a different verdict than the registry. Any fix to the gate cascade is therefore not observable end-to-end without also reasoning about which of the five writers ran last.
zones.evidence_history: Chain 'Dual verdict-arbitration guards intended to prevent stale writes: MinIO sidecar consensus check (RFC-037 D1) and Postgres read-back validation (RFC-037 D5) ... unresolved into POST-FIX-WAVE3 new zone'; chain 'HR3 boot-time ZDR compliance gate' (same boot-vs-per-call split pattern); chain 'Erasure cascade missing explicit tracking'. Themes: 'Fix-one-instance-miss-the-other duplication ... verdict priority maps were duplicated (_LEDGER_VERDICT_PRIORITY vs _LEDGER_PRIORITY, RFC-037); dual verdict-arbitration CAS guards used inconsistent comparison operators (> vs >=, RFC-037)' and 'Threshold/config tightening repeatedly masquerades as content regression in corpus audits ... live-store verification against actual MinIO state, not just dispatched figures, is required'.
zones.evidence_code: storage/verdict.py:78-190 save_doc_meta - verified by grep that VERDICT_PRIORITY / any priority comparison is absent; the only occurrence of the word 'priority' is docstring line 98 describing Postgres. registry_backfill/backfill.py:145 asserts a CAS guard in save_doc_meta that does not exist. worker/registry_mirror.py:150-175: upsert_doc CAS then 'best-effort sidecar backfill with the winning Postgres values', a second write to the same key. client/indexer.py:1302 (tree) and ~1141 (flat) call save_doc_meta from the child process. registry/queries.py:86-127 defines _UPSERT_VERDICT_CAS and _UPSERT_VERDICT_OVERRIDE as two alternative UPDATE bodies selected at queries.py:155. Additional writers: registry_backfill/reconcile.py:76-82, registry_backfill/backfill.py:161 and :323, promotion_sweep.py:124 and :141.

zones.name: Config-layer bifurcation: frozen snapshot vs live os.environ
zones.description: config.py builds a frozen PipelineConfig snapshot from 88 env reads at import time, asserts cross-flag coupling invariants against it, and serializes a subset into every sidecar as the effective_config audit trail. But 55 further os.environ/os.getenv reads live in 24 other modules, several of them re-reading the very same variables at call time with different parsing rules. The recorded audit trail can therefore describe a configuration that did not govern the run.
zones.mechanism: Three verified divergences. (1) pipeline_config.bidi_coherence_enforce is defined (config.py:397, 506) and is included in the sidecar effective_config field list (config.py:705) but has zero consumers; the gate it supposedly controls reads os.environ directly with different truthiness semantics - _envbool accepts {'1','true','yes'} while gates.py:162 requires exactly 'true'. Setting BIDI_COHERENCE_ENFORCE=1 records enforce=True in the sidecar while disabling Gate 7 at runtime. (2) LEAF_SPLIT_RATIO is snapshotted into pipeline_config.leaf_split_ratio and is the subject of an import-time coupling assertion (config.py:597-600, PASS_MAX_LEAF_RATIO <= LEAF_SPLIT_RATIO), yet tree_split.py:385 re-reads float(os.environ.get('LEAF_SPLIT_RATIO','0.30')) at call time - so the assertion guards a value the splitter does not use, and the invariant chain PASS_MAX_LEAF_RATIO <= LEAF_SPLIT_RATIO <= HARD_FAIL_MAX_LEAF_RATIO is unenforceable in the code path that matters. (3) PRE_GARBLE_FORCE_OCR_ENABLED is snapshotted at config.py:488 and independently re-read at indexer.py:530. Because pipeline_config is frozen at import while the direct reads are live, a process that mutates os.environ (tests, the converters_cli child inheriting a modified environment) gets two different answers from the same variable. This is what makes threshold refactors look like content regressions: the audit artifact and the executing code disagree.
zones.evidence_history: Chain 'Zone 7 config-layering fix (commit 610d078): refactored frozen threshold constants from local scopes into a unified _CONFIG scope, revealing that DEPTH_ADEQUACY_FLOOR and CHAR_FLOOR had drifted by 1-2 units across duplicated calls ... changed verdict outcomes for ~20 documents'. Themes: 'Hardcoded constants and fallback boolean flags scattered across files cause invisible asymmetries and prevent unified testing ... Unified config layer (Zone 7) partially addressed this but coverage is incomplete'; 'Threshold/config tightening repeatedly masquerades as content regression in corpus audits: Run-20's D4 pre-publish live-store re-verification found that reported structural collapses (505->80 nodes) were in fact unchanged trees whose verdict flipped purely because a config-layering refactor (610d078) silently raised depth-adequacy or char-floor thresholds'; 'Audit/measurement tooling shares the same blind spots as the code it audits'. config.py carries 51 commits, the highest of any file examined.
zones.evidence_code: config.py:353 _envbool returns membership in ('1','true','yes'); helpers/gates.py:162 'if os.environ.get("BIDI_COHERENCE_ENFORCE", "true").lower() != "true": return (False, "")'. grep confirms bidi_coherence_enforce has no consumer outside config.py itself (definition at :397, assignment at :506, sidecar field list at :705). config.py:511 leaf_split_ratio=float(os.environ.get('LEAF_SPLIT_RATIO','0.30')) and config.py:597-600 assertion, versus helpers/tree_split.py:382-386 which re-reads both LEAF_CONCENTRATION_PARAGRAPH_SPLIT_ENABLED (with a different false-set {'false','0','no','off'}) and LEAF_SPLIT_RATIO. config.py:488 vs client/indexer.py:529-530 for PRE_GARBLE_FORCE_OCR_ENABLED. Counts: 88 os.environ.get in config.py, 55 in 24 other modules. config.py:686-728 builds the effective_config sidecar payload from the frozen dataclass only.

zones.name: Ordered-policy converter chain with load-bearing branch order
zones.description: The PDF converter fallback chain resolves each failure through a five-way if/elif ladder producing a ConverterFailurePolicy (RETRY / BLOCK_AGPL / GATE_AGPL_STRUCTURAL / REJECT / WALK). The classification order is explicitly documented as load-bearing, and the licensing guarantee (HR4: never walk into an AGPL converter on a transient outage) depends entirely on that order - which the RETRY branch defeats.
zones.mechanism: The ladder at indexer.py:670-677 tests RETRY first: 'if _is_transient and _transient_attempts < CONVERTER_TRANSIENT_RETRY_COUNT'. The RETRY handler's comment claims it will 'rewind idx so the for-loop re-enters this entry', but the implementation is a bare `continue` inside `for idx, entry in enumerate(chain)` - which advances to the NEXT chain entry, not the same one. With the shipped default CONVERTER_TRANSIENT_RETRY_COUNT=1 (config.py:522), the first transient failure of the primary converter therefore always walks one step down the chain, and if the next entry is the AGPL converter it executes it - bypassing the BLOCK_AGPL branch that exists precisely to prevent that, because BLOCK_AGPL is only reachable once _transient_attempts has been exhausted. The 'no retry actually happened' bug and the 'HR4 licensing guarantee is unenforced' bug are the same line. More generally, the zone's shape is the generator: policy is derived by falling through an ordered predicate ladder over four independent inputs (_is_transient, _transient_attempts, next_is_agpl, next_idx >= len(chain)) with two orthogonal env toggles (ALLOW_AGPL_FALLBACK removes AGPL entries from the chain and also disables the fitz pre-garble probe; AGPL_STRUCTURAL_FALLBACK_ENABLED gates only the structural walk), so inserting or reordering any branch silently redefines the others. The same ALLOW_AGPL_FALLBACK toggle couples licensing to detection quality: turning it off disables the D3a pre-garble probe and page-count/landscape capture entirely (indexer.py:479-484), which in turn disables Gate 10 (SUSPECT_DENSITY, which only fires when page_count is populated).
zones.evidence_history: Chain 'allow_agpl_fallback gating and AGPL_FALLBACK_TOTAL metric added to prevent silent route-through to AGPL converters ... ISS-35 (2026-07-15) partial fix regressed at POST-FIX-WAVE3 (2026-08-28) because the gating is a binary toggle, not a toggle+remediation'; chain 'AGPL converter structural failures fell through silently without gating or metrics (RFC-018 P2)'; chain 'JOB_TIMEOUT raised to 3630s (RFC-028) and the 16.5x inspector multiplier calibrated (RFC-032)'; chain 'PDF_INSPECTOR_PRECLASSIFY confidence gate (RFC-031/032)'. Themes: 'Remote/external-service code drift is a repeated generative mechanism ... no version/contract pinning pattern appears in Docling, PDF Inspector and arq' and 'Silent degradation patterns: failures fall through unnamed else branches without metrics or gates ... Converter structural failures in route_and_extract (RFC-018) have no explicit handling'. indexer.py carries 17 commits.
zones.evidence_code: client/indexer.py:657-661 comment: 'Ordering is load-bearing: the AGPL branches must be classified BEFORE the generic end-of-chain/WALK branches, or a structural failure into an AGPL converter would fall through to the bare else (its former, ungated behavior).' client/indexer.py:670-677 the ladder; client/indexer.py:692-702 the RETRY handler whose comment says 'rewind idx so the for-loop re-enters this entry' but whose only control-flow statement is `continue` - the loop variable idx is bound by enumerate() and cannot be rewound. config.py:521-522 CONVERTER_TRANSIENT_RETRY_COUNT default '1'. client/indexer.py:479-484 'D3a pre-conversion probe skipped ... ALLOW_AGPL_FALLBACK=false blocks fitz' - the same branch that populates state.pdf_page_count, which helpers/gates.py:227-243 requires for Gate 10.

zones.name: Recovery dispatch: tuple-keyed dedup and unguarded raising normalizers
zones.description: The GateSpec recovery loop deduplicates by the recovery_fns tuple rather than by individual method name, so a method listed in two different tuples runs twice; none of the OCR recovery methods check whether full-page OCR has already been applied. Separately, ensure_tessdata was converted from a silent-fallback helper into a raising one, but two of its four call sites sit outside any try block, converting a language-availability problem into a terminal job error with no persisted artifact.
zones.mechanism: gates.py declares NODE_COUNT_LOW with recovery_fns=('_recover_low_content_ocr','_recover_image_dominant_ocr') and DEPTH_LOW with recovery_fns=('_recover_image_dominant_ocr',). The loop's dedup set is typed set[tuple[str, ...]] and tests `_gate.recovery_fns in _fired_recovery`, so these two distinct tuples both fire and _recover_image_dominant_ocr executes twice for any document where both gates fire - which is the common case, since a tree with node_count<3 almost always has depth<2. Each execution is a full-page OCR re-extraction of the whole PDF. The methods guard only on `state.ok or ext != '.pdf'` plus their own flag; _execute_ocr_retry never consults state.full_page_already_applied even though three callers set it. Combined with GARBLING/NODE_GARBLING's shared tuple (correctly deduped) this yields up to three full-page OCR passes per document, which is the direct mechanism behind jobs timing out before save_doc and leaving zero MinIO artifact. The second half of the zone: ensure_tessdata now raises TessdataUnavailableError for unavailable non-Latin scripts. Inside _execute_ocr_retry it is caught by the broad `except Exception` and degrades to a metric, but at indexer.py:885 (the image-extension branch) it is called bare, so a .jpg requesting an unavailable script raises out of index(), is classified by worker/errors.py as 'converter_env_missing' terminal, and the document ends as ERROR with nothing persisted - a strictly worse outcome than the MARGINAL it previously received. Two call sites, two opposite failure semantics, from one behaviour change.
zones.evidence_history: Chain 'ocr_langs.py fix #2 (commit cf904ff / RFC-040 D5): ensure_tessdata now raises TessdataUnavailableError instead of silently substituting deu/eng ... the labor-distribution pie-chart .jpg went MARGINAL->ERROR (job times out before save_doc, zero MinIO artifact)'; chain '_OCR_ESCALATION single kill-switch ... RFC-018 P1/P3 remain unresolved through POST-FIX-WAVE3, meaning the kill-switch is still a single point of failure with no observability gate'; chain 'OCR recovery eligibility check only inspected first_defect'; chain 'JOB_TIMEOUT raised to 3630s (RFC-028)'. Themes: 'Multi-site fixes that consistently miss 1-2 locations, requiring follow-up commits and AST guards' and 'Compensating heuristics are repeatedly substituted for the actual proposed fix, then themselves become entrenched'. recovery.py carries 13 commits.
zones.evidence_code: helpers/gates.py:368-386 GateSpec(NODE_COUNT_LOW, recovery_fns=('_recover_low_content_ocr','_recover_image_dominant_ocr')) vs GateSpec(DEPTH_LOW, recovery_fns=('_recover_image_dominant_ocr',)). client/indexer.py:1454-1459: '_fired_recovery: set[tuple[str, ...]] = set()' and 'if not _gate.recovery_fns or _gate.recovery_fns in _fired_recovery: continue' - dedup is on the tuple, not the member. client/recovery.py:458-498 _recover_image_dominant_ocr guards only on state.ok / ext / flag / image-line ratio. client/recovery.py:232-236 _execute_ocr_retry docstring mentions full_page_already_applied only as something 'callers should set'; the function never reads it. client/indexer.py:885 'img_langs = await asyncio.to_thread(ensure_tessdata, detect_ocr_langs(filename))' with no enclosing try, versus client/recovery.py:273 inside the try whose except at :375 swallows it. converters/ocr_langs.py:123,161,174,186 raise sites. worker/errors.py:30 maps TessdataUnavailableError -> ChildErrorClassification('converter_env_missing', terminal=True).

zones.name: Divergent parallel garble/text accessors
zones.description: Garble is decided by three procedures that were meant to be consolidated into one but were not: detect_garble (the declared 'sole public entry point'), a raw garble_prongs call inside _garble_check_nodes' whole-tree fallback, and _garble_check_flat_blocks. The same shape recurs in flat-block text extraction, where role-typed blocks omit the 'text' key and three separate accessors each re-implement the role dispatch.
zones.mechanism: detect_garble wraps garble_prongs with real policy: it re-infers the dominant script when None, applies the RFC-025 D2 short-text rule, selects a normalization blob kind, and - critically - runs a presentation-forms RECOVERY heuristic that can flip _had_pf from False to True (garble.py:577-587). The whole-tree fallback inside _garble_check_nodes (garble.py:747-757) bypasses all of that: it calls normalize_for_garble then garble_prongs directly, passing script_context.had_presentation_forms through verbatim. The aggregate path is therefore strictly less sensitive to exactly the signal RFC-040 D5 was about, and the two procedures cannot be kept in sync by construction - only by a reviewer noticing. The flat side repeats it: helpers/flat.py emits blocks where role=='table' and role=='image' carry no 'text' key by design (RFC-022 B3), and _flat_block_primary_text (flat.py:175-197), _flat_search_text (flat.py:200-220) and the table-branch at flat.py:242 each contain their own role dispatch to recover the missing content. The Zone-9 header-only-table fix had to be applied inside _flat_block_primary_text alone; any measurement or audit path that reads block['text'] directly still registers zero table content. This is the structural reason 'fix one instance, miss the other' recurs: the codebase has no single choke point for 'text of a thing', only a family of near-identical accessors each of which is a valid place to add a fix.
zones.evidence_history: Chain 'Garble detection consolidation: duplicate tree/flat implementations merged into a single garble_check_nodes guard. Previously _tree_is_garbled and _flat_text_is_garbled had drifted (ISS-36); RFC-040 D3/D6 consolidation eliminates one branch ... marked partial'; chain 'route_and_extract_flat's table-role blocks intentionally omit a text key by design (RFC-022 B3), so measurement tooling that counts text key presence will register zero table content ... unresolved through POST-FIX-WAVE3'; chain 'garble.py fix #1'; chain 'Wave 2 triage spec for garble-detection kernel marked as redundant ... digit-ratio floor duplication'. Themes: 'Fix-one-instance-miss-the-other duplication is a chronic, cross-cutting defect generator: the garble digit-ratio floor was duplicated between _tree_is_garbled/_flat_text_is_garbled (ISS-36) and again between garble_prongs and _garble_check_nodes fallback (RFC-040 2a)' and 'Shared choke points ... garble_check_nodes is called from both tree validation and flat extraction; a fix to one path does not reach the other'. garble.py carries 9 commits and 5 distinct Zone-N labels.
zones.evidence_code: helpers/garble.py:529-540 detect_garble docstring: 'Unified garble evaluation entry point (Zone-3). Single-surface API: all garble heuristics ... run inside garble_prongs.' Contradicted by helpers/garble.py:745-757, the _is_toplevel fallback which calls normalize_for_garble + garble_prongs directly, skipping the _had_pf recovery at helpers/garble.py:577-587 and the short-text rule at :565-571. Third procedure at helpers/garble.py:766+ _garble_check_flat_blocks. helpers/flat.py:87-95 and :116-126 construct table/image blocks with no 'text' key; helpers/flat.py:184-197 (_flat_block_primary_text, carrying the Zone-9 header-only-table fix), :205-216 (_flat_search_text) and :242 each re-implement the role dispatch independently.

zones.name: Order-coupled erasure manifest with implicit inter-step data flow
zones.description: The HR2 right-to-erasure cascade was refactored into a declarative _ERASURE_MANIFEST of eleven ErasureStep entries driven by a generic loop, which reads as order-independent. It is not: two steps discover data that later steps require, so reordering or removing an entry silently converts a purge into a no-op that reports success.
zones.mechanism: ErasureContext is mutable state threaded through the manifest, and two fields are discovered mid-cascade rather than up front. ctx.doc_name is recovered inside _erase_uploads (step 1) from the uploads listing when the processed artifact is already gone; steps 5 (hash_cache) and 7 (preloaded) are unreachable without it and merely log a warning and return False. ctx.sha256 is read inside _erase_verdicts (step 2d) from processed/<id>.meta.json, which step 3 then deletes - so the verdict ledger at verdicts/<sha256>.json can only ever be purged if 2d runs before 3. Both dependencies are documented only in prose ('Must run before the sidecar is deleted (step 3) because the sha256 that keys the ledger lives only in processed/<doc_id>.meta.json') and in the manifest's ordering; there is no assertion, no dependency declaration, and the driver comment actively invites reordering ('Adding a derived store is a one-line entry here plus its _erase_* coroutine; the driver in delete_doc needs no change'). Compounding this, the steps that most often fail to reach their store are marked required=False - verdicts, preloaded, figures, flat_json - so an unreached ledger purge is logged at DEBUG as an 'expected miss' and delete_doc returns {'errors': []}, i.e. an apparently clean HR2 cascade with a residual PII-derived artifact. The generative property: every new derived store added to the pipeline inherits the blind spot automatically, because compliance is enforced by list order and a required flag rather than by the write-path registration.

Themes: 'HR2 (erasure) and HR3 (PII/ZDR egress) compliance gaps recur every time a new storage location or new LLM call site is introduced: ISS-02 fixed erasure in the happy path registry delete; ISS-41 found the same gap in a parallel _cleanup_artifact path ... New storage or new LLM paths automatically inherit the old blind spots without triggering a codebase-wide audit' and 'Multi-site fixes that consistently miss 1-2 locations'.
